market.conclusion: Tech is in a downtrend. QQQ is below both its 50- and 200-day averages, and only 8% of stocks are above their 50-day average. Fear is elevated and credit spreads are widening, so this is a time to be patient with short-term trades and selective about long-term buys.
arguments: Macro: the tech market is in a downtrend, the VIX is elevated at 26.8, and credit spreads widened from 3.18 to 3.72 over four weeks. I give this the most weight, because it is the one view that every stock shares.

Technical: SPY and QQQ are making lower highs and lower lows, and chips have lagged badly (SMH trailed QQQ by 12.7 points). The latest one-day bounces don't break that pattern, so I treat them as noise until resistance is cleared.
Fundamental: several quality businesses are now cheap (NVDA, NFLX, ORCL). That matters for a years-long view but does little against the trend over the next few weeks.
Quant: no signal type is validated, and 0 of 928 forecasts have been scored. I give it no weight.

Trading conditions are RED with 1 of 5 checks passing. This rule is experimental and restricts nothing, so I treat it as background only. Defensive sectors such as XLP and XLU are beating tech, which fits the caution.
market.change_mind: A daily close above $664.43 on QQQ, or above $745.75 on SPY, would turn me less cautious. The 2026-12-04 jobs report is the next big event for the whole market.

deep_dive.case_for: It has a grade A business, revenue up 83.38% over the last 12 months, a forward P/E of 8.99, and a price-to-sales ratio near the bottom of its own 5-year range. At $150.49 it trades below its whole value range of $194.80–$411.04, and earnings estimates rose 4.34% in 30 days.
deep_dive.case_against: The chart is a downtrend: the stock is down 29.57% in 20 days and sits well below both its 50- and 200-day averages, right on support at $147.19–$150.41. Its 65% operating margin is at a 5-year peak, unpaid customer bills are growing faster than sales, and insiders sold $946.6M outside pre-set plans. A headline also reports that Nvidia halted chip shipments to south-east Asia (unverified).
deep_dive.decides: For the long term, the business numbers decide it, so build a position gradually rather than all at once. For the swing, the levels decide it: a close above $171.50 is the sign of strength, and a close below $147.19 means more downside first.
